objectives: Hear and identify short /e/ in simple CVC words.
Distinguish short /e/ from familiar short vowels.
Connect the /e/ phoneme to the grapheme e.
Apply the sound-to-print connection in controlled CVC examples.
concepts: Short /e/ is a middle vowel phoneme in words such as bed, hen, pen, and ten.
Vowel discrimination depends on listening to the middle phoneme.
The grapheme e represents short /e/ in these taught CVC patterns.

definitions.definition: The short vowel sound heard in words such as bed and hen.
The smallest sound unit that can change meaning in a word.
A letter or group of letters used to represent a sound.

workedExamples: bed versus bid → isolate the middle vowel and listen for /e/ or /i/.
commonMistakes: Choosing a vowel from the word shape without listening.
Naming the letter without producing the sound.
keyTakeaways: Short /e/ is heard in bed, hen, pen and ten.
Connect /e/ to the printed letter e.
Use sound-by-sound decoding rather than guessing.

basic: Identify short /e/ in spoken and printed CVC words.
conceptual: Explain how the middle vowel changes between short /e/ and short /i/.
application: Map the middle /e/ sound to the letter e in CVC words.
higherOrderThinking: Select the correct vowel after comparing minimal contrasts.
mixedReview: Mix short /e/ recognition with previously taught vowel discrimination.

quickRevision: Hear /e/ → identify e → read the CVC word.
mistakeBasedRevision: If /e/ is confused with /i/, isolate and stretch the middle vowel before choosing the grapheme.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat auditory contrast and sound-to-print mapping for short /e/.

outcomes: Learner identifies short /e/ in taught CVC words.
Learner distinguishes short /e/ from short /i/ and other familiar short vowels in controlled contrasts.
Learner connects short /e/ to the grapheme e.
Learner begins decoding short-/e/ CVC words through sound-by-sound blending.
